blocks.title: What Cisco does
blocks.text: Cisco designs and sells hardware, software, and AI-powered digital infrastructure; it operates globally and manages the business by geography.

evidence.quote: Cisco designs and sells a broad range of technologies including hardware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) powered digital infrastructure

blocks.title: How it sells
blocks.text: Sales are direct and indirect; a substantial portion is sold through channel partners.

evidence.quote: A substantial portion of our products and services is sold indirectly through channel partners

blocks.title: Revenue model
blocks.text: The portfolio includes hardware, software licenses, SaaS, subscriptions, and services.

evidence.quote: software licenses and software-as-a-service (SaaS) offerings

cells: Switching, routing, wireless, and servers for building, securing, automating, and modernizing network infrastructure.

evidence.quote: switching, routing, wireless, and servers

cells: Network security, identity and access management, SASE, and threat prevention, detection, and response.

evidence.quote: spans Network Security, Identity and Access Management, Secure Access Service Edge (SASE)

cells: Software and devices for distributed-team collaboration and customer and employee interactions.

evidence.quote: technology that enables distributed teams to collaborate effortlessly

cells: Telemetry and network assurance to assess service health, application performance, and digital experience.

evidence.quote: connect insights across AI agents, applications, infrastructure, networks and digital experience

cells: Technical support, planning, design, implementation, and consulting.

evidence.quote: planning, design, implementation and high-value consulting

blocks.title: AI infrastructure applications
blocks.text: Cisco says it provides network infrastructure for AI training and inference workloads for hyperscalers and enterprises.

evidence.quote: We provide network infrastructure to power AI training and inference workloads for both hyperscalers and enterprises.

cells: Identified by Cisco as one of its three primary customer markets.

evidence.quote: Our customers primarily operate in the following markets: enterprise, public sector and service provider and cloud.

cells: Includes federal, state and local governments and educational institutions.

evidence.quote: Public Sector includes federal, state and local governments, as well as educational institution customers.

cells: Includes carriers, hyperscalers, Internet, cable, wireless, media, broadcast, and content providers.

evidence.quote: includes regional, national, and international wireline carriers and hyperscalers

cells: Total product orders increased 35% year over year; up 25% excluding hyperscalers.

evidence.quote: Q4 total product orders up 35% year over year; up 25% excluding hyperscalers

cells: Networking product orders increased 40% year over year.

evidence.quote: Networking product orders grew 40% year over year in Q4

blocks.title: Documented facts and inferred buyer archetypes

cells: Channel partners include systems integrators, service providers, other third-party resellers, and distributors.

evidence.quote: Channel partners include systems integrators, service providers, other third-party resellers, and distributors.

evidence.quote: We primarily sell to public sector customers through a network of third-party application and technology vendors and channel partners.

cells: Systems integrators typically sell directly to end users and may provide integration, installation, and support.

cells: Enterprise infrastructure or IT teams evaluating network modernization and AI workload infrastructure.

evidence.quote: We provide network infrastructure to power AI training and inference workloads for both hyperscalers and enterprises.
